sentences.text: Social worker Tom Okafor from Harbridge adult services visited Harold Pryce at his home on Monday 16 November 2026.
Harold Pryce lives alone in a house he bought with his first wife Joan in 1971; his second wife Sandra is currently at her sister's house.
Harold and Sandra have been married for nine years; Sandra is his second wife, while his first wife Joan died in 2013.
Harold has a stick and a frame upstairs and had a fall in the garden in the spring; he has not had any falls since.
Harold washes himself by sitting on a stool in the shower but finds putting on socks difficult.
Sandra cooks meals; Harold can make a sandwich.
Harold reported that there is no toilet upstairs.
Sandra manages Harold's medication and keeps it in her handbag; she does not always give him his tablets.
Harold stated that he does not want Sandra in trouble, but he wants the abuse to stop and he wants his tablets.
Harold stated that Carol never liked Sandra and that he would tell Carol about the abuse, though he acknowledged she would be upset.
Harold stated that he was sorry for the 'fuss' regarding the disclosure of abuse.
Social worker Tom Okafor stated that Harold did nothing to be sorry for and did the right thing by disclosing the abuse.
Harold disclosed that Sandra hits him with her walking stick when she gets cross.
Harold stated that Sandra hits him with her walking stick on his arms when she is cross.
Harold reported that Sandra hits him once a week, or more often if she has had a bad day.
Harold disclosed that Sandra locks him in the bedroom when she goes out, claiming it is so he does not fall.
Harold stated that Sandra locks him in the bedroom two or three times a week for the afternoon.
Harold disclosed that if he annoys Sandra, she keeps his tablets back; last week he did not have his heart tablets for three days.
Harold stated that he has missed his heart tablets for three days a few times in the past and also missed his water tablets.
Harold stated that Sandra says she would take the house if he left.
Harold stated that the house is in his name only, but Sandra claims she would get it if he went away.
Harold stated that he felt safe that night because Sandra was going to her sister's house the next day.
Social worker Tom Okafor offered the number for the older people's advocacy service and instructed Harold to ring 999 if he is ever hurt or locked in.
Harold's daughter Carol lives in Kestwick, about two hours away, and calls him on Sundays.
Harold stated that his pension goes into a joint account with Sandra, who does the bills, while he keeps his own savings in a book at the post office.
Harold stated that he has a mobile phone that Carol made him get.
Social worker Tom Okafor proposed raising a safeguarding concern with the team, arranging for Harold's tablets to be delivered in a blister pack from the chemist, and contacting a
Social worker Tom Okafor proposed contacting Carol by Friday and referring Harold to an occupational therapist for assistance with socks and stairs.
Social worker Tom Okafor proposed to return on Tuesday 1 December in the morning, noting that Sandra would be at her sister's house.
